subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

Qatar has extended strict quarantine rules having required travellers to isolate for up to 14 days upon their arrival in the country.
solution:
The error is having required travellers; use requiring travellers.

"Having required" shows an action completed before the main verb, but the rules require isolation now, at the same time as the extension. A present participle (or "that require") expresses this.

Correct sentence: Qatar has extended strict quarantine rules requiring travellers to isolate for up to 14 days upon their arrival in the country.
conceptTested: Use of present participle to denote simultaneous actions instead of a prior completed action implied by a perfect participle.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.

The child requested his mother to gave him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat.

options.A: The child requested his mother to
options.B: gave him a big chocolate because he
options.C: had been very good all day
options.a: The child requested his mother to
options.b: gave him a big chocolate because he
options.c: had been very good all day

solution:
The error is in part B: to gave should be to give.

The infinitive marker “to” is followed by the base form of the verb: requested his mother to give.

Correct sentence: The child requested his mother to give him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat.
conceptTested: The infinitive marker 'to' must be followed by the base form (V1) of the verb.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

The psychological bareness (1)/ of her narrative (2)/ precludes any embellishment, yet render (3)/ the structure more profoundly intimate. (4)
solution:
Rule: The subject "The psychological bareness" is singular, so both verbs joined by "yet" must be singular: "precludes ... yet renders".
So the error is in part (3): "render" should be "renders".
Correct sentence: The psychological bareness of her narrative precludes any embellishment, yet renders the structure more profoundly intimate.
conceptTested: Compound predicates joined by coordinating conjunctions like 'yet' must agree in number and form with the singular subject.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

Can you borrow your book to me just for one day?
solution:
Rule: Lend means to give something for a time; borrow means to take something for a time. When you ask someone to give you their book, the correct verb is lend ("lend something to someone").

So the error is in "borrow your".

Correct sentence: Can you lend your book to me just for one day?
conceptTested: Distinction between 'borrow' (to take) and 'lend' (to give temporarily).

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
The following sentence has been divided into three parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation errors, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.

(A) The investigation revealed that the culprit, / (B) rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough / (C) to have been taunted the victims during the trial. / (D) No Error

options.A: The investigation revealed that the culprit
options.B: rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough
options.C: to have been taunted the victims during the trial
options.a: The investigation revealed that the culprit
options.b: rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough
options.c: to have been taunted the victims during the trial

solution:
Rule: "The victims" is the object of "taunt", so the active perfect infinitive (to have + V³) is needed. The passive "to have been taunted" cannot take an object here.

So the error is in part (C).

Correct sentence: The investigation revealed that the culprit, rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough to have taunted the victims during the trial.
conceptTested: Use of the active perfect infinitive (to have + V3) when an object follows, rather than the passive infinitive.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

Much of the guidelines (1)/ pertaining to AI governance (2)/ were based on speculative models (3)/ and industry projections. (4)
solution:
Rule: Much is used with uncountable nouns; many is used with plural countable nouns.

'Guidelines' is a plural countable noun, so 'Much of the guidelines' must be 'Many of the guidelines'. The plural verb 'were' then agrees correctly.

Correct sentence: Many of the guidelines pertaining to AI governance were based on speculative models and industry projections.
conceptTested: Usage of 'Much' (with uncountable nouns) versus 'Many' (with plural countable nouns).

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Spot the error in the below-given sentence.

'She can sings very well'.
solution:
Rule: A modal verb (can, could, may, must, will, shall ...) is always followed by the base form of the verb.

'can sings' is wrong; it should be 'can sing'.

Correct sentence: She can sing very well.
conceptTested: Modal verbs (can, could, may, must, will, shall) are always followed by the base form (V1) of the verb without adding 's' or 'es'.

subject: English Comprehension

options.A: Mitali's hair is long and black.
options.B: Either of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties.
options.C: One of the cars in the garage is fifty years old.
options.D: Sharon has shared her devastating grief after the sudden death of her 57-year-old brother.
options.a: Mitali's hair is long and black.
options.b: Either of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties.
options.c: One of the cars in the garage is fifty years old.
options.d: Sharon has shared her devastating grief after the sudden death of her 57-year-old brother.

solution:
The sentence marked incorrect is 'Either of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties.'

Rule: Either means 'one of two'. When the number of choices is not limited to two, any of is used instead: 'Any of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties.'

Sentence 1 (hair takes a singular verb), sentence 3 (one of + plural noun + singular verb) and sentence 4 are correct.
conceptTested: Distinction between 'Either' (used for one of two choices) and 'Any' (used when choices exceed two).
